title: Native engineering workbench with shared Rust core
summary: Tauri desktop and JSON CLI share repository inspection and engineering action logic, with a React/TypeScript interface.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Built a Tauri 2 engineering workbench with a React/TypeScript UI and shared Rust application core consumed by both the desktop interface and a JSON CLI.
Implemented bounded asynchronous repository inspection, separating expensive Git refreshes from independent process-state updates.
Hardened registered engineering actions through identifier/slot/argument validation, environment controls and timeouts; direct actions launch argument arrays without a shell.
Delegated renderer operations to the existing workspace implementation rather than duplicating project runtime behavior.
Bound repository-inspection concurrency to four asynchronous tasks, then restore stable display ordering; keep renderer status updates separate from expensive dashboard Git refreshes.

Designed independent CPU/GPU controls and packaged-build/process views using React, TypeScript and TanStack Query, with targeted cache updates, build progress/error feedback and event-driven packaged-state invalidation.

notes: Bounded concurrency is an implemented responsiveness strategy, not a measured latency/speedup result. Cross-platform Rust structure does not prove every desktop action is supported or tested on every host; development renderer actions explicitly use a macOS backend.
